title: Multi-tenant event streaming platform
description: Teams publish and consume events on a shared Confluent Cloud backbone. Kafka Connect, run by Confluent for Kubernetes on EKS, brings in database changes and HTTP requests and writes to S3, all over a private link. Flink turns them into each tenant's output topics. Everything is requested through a portal and delivered by Terraform and GitHub Actions.

detail.role: Where a team asks for a topic, a connector, a schema or a service account. The request becomes a pull request, never a ticket.
detail.why: Teams get what they need in minutes and the platform team stops being a queue. Every request is reviewed code.
detail.tradeoff: The portal has to be kept as current as the platform; a request it cannot express goes back to a ticket.

security.text: The portal holds no cluster credentials. It only opens pull requests, so every change is reviewed and recorded.

detail.role: The single source of truth for every topic, schema, service account, role binding and connector.
detail.why: What is in the repository is what exists. Drift is a diff, and a rollback is a revert.

detail.role: Validates each pull request (naming, quotas, schema compatibility, policy), then runs Terraform on merge.
detail.why: Rules are checked before anything is created, not after.

security.text: Pipelines get short-lived cloud credentials through OIDC. No long-lived keys sit in the repository or the runner.

detail.role: Creates and changes the Confluent Cloud resources (clusters, topics, service accounts, role bindings, connectors) and the AWS and Kubernetes side.
detail.why: One tool and one state for both clouds, with a plan that is reviewed before it is applied.
detail.tradeoff: State is a secret-bearing asset and must itself be locked down and backed up.

security.text: Plan runs read-only. Apply runs with a narrower, separate role, and only on the protected branch.

detail.role: Maps the claims in a client's token or certificate to an identity pool, and the pool to roles on specific topics, groups and connectors.
detail.why: Access follows the workload's identity, not a shared secret, and each tenant sees only its own resources.

security.text: No identity pool has any role until it is bound, and each binding is scoped to one tenant's topic prefix.

detail.role: Issues the signed tokens that workloads and engineers present. Their claims (tenant, team, environment) feed the identity pools.
detail.why: One place to say who a workload is, and one place to revoke it.

security.text: Tokens expire in minutes and are checked on every connection. Nothing is trusted because of where it runs.

detail.role: Issues and rotates the client and server certificates used for mutual TLS between tenants, Connect and the clusters.
detail.why: Both ends prove who they are on every connection, so a stolen network position is not enough.

security.text: Certificates are short-lived and renewed by automation; a leaked one stops working within hours.

detail.role: The systems of record that teams want to turn into event streams. Debezium reads their change logs.
detail.why: No change to the application: the stream is built from the database's own log.

risks.text: An idle consumer lets the database keep its change log and fill its disk. Slot lag needs an alert.

detail.role: Teams' services that call in with requests, or that the platform calls out to with results.
detail.why: Services that do not speak Kafka can still join a stream.

detail.role: Where tenants land stream data for analytics and long-term retention.
detail.why: Cheap storage that outlives topic retention.

security.text: Each tenant writes to its own prefix through a role that can reach nothing else.

cost.text: Pay for stored data; the Connect workers are already running.

detail.role: Applications that read their pipeline's output topics.
detail.why: Each team consumes only the streams it has been granted.

security.text: A consumer identity can read its granted topics and its own consumer group, nothing else.

detail.role: Applications that publish events into their tenant's topics.
detail.why: Teams publish facts as they happen and never wait on a consumer.

security.text: Each producer connects with its own certificate and is held to its tenant's throughput quota.

detail.role: Read each database's change log and turn every insert, update and delete into an event.
detail.why: Captures changes with no extra load on the application and no missed rows.
detail.tradeoff: Schema changes in the source database must be handled deliberately, or the connector stops.

detail.role: The source connector turns incoming HTTP requests into events. The sink connector calls an HTTP endpoint for each event and can return the response to a topic.
detail.why: Request/response systems join the event platform without custom glue code.
detail.tradeoff: A slow downstream endpoint slows the sink; retries and a dead-letter topic are needed.

risks.text: One tenant's slow endpoint can fill a Connect task. Per-connector timeouts, retries and a dead-letter topic contain it.

detail.role: Writes topic data to S3 in batches, one connector per tenant.
detail.why: Archival and analytics get the data without a second pipeline.

detail.role: Runs Connect (and any other Confluent component) as Kubernetes resources: declare a connector, and the operator makes it so.
detail.why: Rolling upgrades, certificate wiring and scaling are handled by the operator, not by hand.

security.text: Connector credentials are Kubernetes secrets mounted into the worker. They are never written into the connector definition.

detail.role: The worker pool that runs every connector. It reads from and writes to Kafka over the private link.
detail.why: One shared, scalable runtime instead of a process per integration.
detail.tradeoff: Tenants share workers, so tasks are limited per connector and noisy connectors are moved to their own worker pool.

security.text: Each tenant's connectors use their own service account and their own topic prefix.

cost.text: Connectors share one pool of nodes, so the idle cost of a connector is close to zero.

detail.role: The private connection from the platform VPC to Confluent Cloud. Traffic never crosses the public internet.
detail.why: No public endpoint to attack, and a network path that can be allowed in exactly one direction.

security.text: The cluster's public endpoint is disabled. Only this endpoint, from this VPC, can reach it.

detail.role: Stores every topic's schema and enforces compatibility rules before a producer can change it.
detail.why: Consumers are not broken by a producer's change, and the contract is written down.

security.text: A producer that breaks compatibility is refused at publish time.

detail.role: The shared event backbone. Each tenant has its own topic prefix, its own service accounts and a quota.
detail.why: Replicated across three zones, so losing a zone loses no data and no availability.
detail.tradeoff: A shared cluster means shared limits. Large tenants get their own cluster when a quota is not enough.

security.text: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, and a role binding required for every read or write.

cost.text: Cost follows provisioned throughput and storage, so a quota doubles as a budget.

risks.text: Partition counts and throughput are shared, so quotas must be enforced per tenant.

detail.role: A second cluster kept in step by cluster linking. Clients can switch to it when the primary is unavailable.
detail.why: A regional outage becomes a switch-over instead of an incident.
detail.tradeoff: A little data can be lost on failover (the link is asynchronous), and the second cluster is paid for while idle.

cost.text: The secondary costs money even when nothing reads from it.

detail.role: Reads input topics, filters, enriches and joins them across sources, and publishes the result to destination topics. There is one such pipeline per use case, and many tenants.
detail.why: Processing is a managed service, so a pipeline is a SQL statement, not a cluster.
detail.tradeoff: Each pipeline holds state, so schema changes and restarts must be planned.

security.text: Each pipeline runs as its own service account and can read and write only its own topics.

cost.text: Billed for compute used by each statement, so idle pipelines cost little.

detail.role: Collects metrics from the operator and the Connect workers: task state, lag, restarts, resource use.
detail.why: Shows whether the integrations are keeping up before a tenant notices.

detail.role: One place for the health of the whole platform: both sides' metrics, per-tenant dashboards and the alerts that page the platform team.
detail.why: One view across Confluent Cloud and Kubernetes, not two tools to flip between.

security.text: Only metrics and logs are sent. Record contents and secrets never leave the platform.

detail.role: Cluster, topic and connector metrics from Confluent Cloud, plus audit logs of who did what.
detail.why: Throughput, lag, consumer-group delay and every access decision are visible.

links.label: Opens pull request
links.detail: A request in the portal becomes a pull request that adds a topic, connector, schema or service account.

links.label: Triggers
links.detail: A change to the repository starts validation, and a merge starts the apply.

links.label: Runs plan and apply
links.detail: The pipeline runs Terraform, with read-only credentials for plan and a narrower role for apply.

links.label: Creates role bindings
links.detail: Terraform creates the service accounts, identity pools and role bindings that give each tenant its access.

links.label: Applies connectors
links.detail: Terraform and the pipeline apply connector and cluster definitions to Kubernetes, where the operator acts on them.

links.label: Claims to pools
links.detail: The identity provider's token claims (tenant, team, environment) select which identity pool, and so which roles, a caller gets.

links.label: Issues client certificates
links.detail: Tenant clients get short-lived certificates for mutual TLS. The same authority issues the certificates the Connect workers and the clusters use.

links.label: Change log
links.detail: Debezium reads the database's transaction log, so the application is not touched.

links.label: Change events
links.detail: Source tasks run in the Connect workers and hand each change to the worker to publish.

links.label: Requests in
links.detail: The HTTP source connector accepts requests from tenant services and publishes them as events; the HTTP sink calls out the other way and can write the response back.

links.label: Runs in
links.detail: The HTTP connectors run as tasks inside the Connect workers.

links.label: Records out
links.detail: The sink task takes records the worker reads from a topic.

links.label: Writes batches
links.detail: Files per time window, under one prefix per tenant, through a role limited to that prefix.

links.label: Deploys and manages
links.detail: The operator creates the worker pool, wires the certificates and rolls upgrades.

links.label: Produce and consume
links.detail: Workers talk to Kafka over mutual TLS, through the private endpoint only.

links.label: Private traffic
links.detail: Kafka traffic arrives at the cluster over the private connection, never the internet.

links.label: Publish events
links.detail: Each producer authenticates with its certificate and identity-pool token and is held to its tenant's quota.

links.label: Subscribe
links.detail: Consumers read only the topics they have been granted, in their own consumer group.

links.label: Consume and publish
links.detail: Flink statements read input topics, filter, enrich and join them, and publish results to the destination topics.

links.label: Cluster link
links.detail: Topics and consumer offsets are mirrored to the secondary region so clients can fail over.

links.label: Schemas
links.detail: Producers and consumers check each message against its registered schema.

links.label: Authorises
links.detail: Every connection is checked against the role bindings before it can read or write.

links.label: Scraped
links.detail: Task state, lag and restarts are scraped from the workers.

links.label: Metrics API
links.detail: Cluster, topic and connector metrics and audit logs.

links.label: Pushes metrics
links.detail: Kubernetes-side metrics go to New Relic.

links.label: Pushes metrics
links.detail: Confluent Cloud metrics and audit logs go to New Relic.

layers.label: Control plane
layers.summary: How things are requested, approved, provisioned and authorised: portal, repository, pipelines, identity and certificates.

layers.label: Tenants
layers.summary: What teams own: their databases, services, producers, consumers and data lake.

layers.label: Data plane
layers.summary: Where events move: Connect on EKS, the private link, the Kafka clusters, Schema Registry and Flink.

layers.label: Observability
layers.summary: Metrics and audit logs from both sides, collected in New Relic.

trace.label: A row changes in a tenant's database
Debezium reads it from the transaction log
A Connect worker takes the change event
It crosses to Confluent Cloud over the private link, with mutual TLS
It lands in the tenant's topic after an authorisation check
A Flink pipeline joins and transforms it
The result is published to the destination topic
